root_task: JWT-local explicit-empty/default/delegation review; preserve original route Actor/caps and global ACL

conclusions.finding: The candidate inserts default into the saved role. Official modern and legacy explicit empty inputs save an empty effective list; default is added to newly issued tokens according to the role flag.

The candidate applies global token-policy assignment validation to JWT role configuration. Official role parsing/storage has no such writer subset gate. Preserve real route capability authorization and remove only this JWT-local call.

Do not replace removed assignment validation with an early root-policy 400. Official role storage and token issuance are separate: source permits storing root configuration and forbids root at token creation. Preserve candidate's existing pre-service/pre-batch login root rejection and issued-token provenance guards.

The candidate lacks a JWT role token_no_default_policy member and rejects the field. A compatible local implementation needs default-false persistence, omitted-update preservation, readback, and official TypeBool decoding, plus common issuance handling for both token types.
Keep existing auth_jwt_renewal.rs byte-for-byte; reapplying role policies or a changed role default flag to existing tokens would introduce a different behavior.

The unchanged original23 and actual executor source do not contain explicit []/root role/default-role flag or login policy cases. They can settle capability/omitted-policy behavior for truly no-default actors; do not promote that result to untested policy semantics.

narrow_proposal.change: JWT role policy parse only: add_default=false, preserve omitted prior list and explicit empty clearing. Leave global policies() byte-identical.
narrow_proposal.reason: Separate role configuration from issued-token default injection.

narrow_proposal.change: Remove only JWT role self.validate_assignment(actor,&role_policies), retaining self.permission on the original create/update capability and the native captured Actor/source capability path.
narrow_proposal.reason: Do not treat a role definition as direct token API policy delegation.

narrow_proposal.change: JWT-local token_no_default_policy: persisted default false; omission on update retains previous; expose on role read. Match official FieldData TypeBool weak decoder rather than assume only JSON booleans; accepted input domain must be separately pinned before candidate freeze.
narrow_proposal.reason: Current whitelist/struct lack the field. Preserve old serialized false/absent meaning and reject only officially invalid values.

narrow_proposal.change: Compute one final issued policy set after genuine JWT/root guards and before branching; clone role policies, add default only when role flag is false. Both service Token and BatchClaims consume this same result. Explicit default is never removed by the flag.
narrow_proposal.reason: Changing storage parsing alone would silently remove expected default policy from both login branches.

narrow_proposal.change: Keep renewal/global validate_assignment/general token issuance and non-JWT auth paths unchanged; do not strip default from existing persisted roles during migration.
narrow_proposal.reason: Previously stored default may be explicit or historical; no evidence permits destructive rewriting.

additional_limits: Official modern/legacy parsing paths differ in normalization, precedence and legacy read alias retention. The narrow empty/default fix is not a blanket claim of complete policy-field representation parity.
Default suppression is distinct from token API no_default_policy used to create the matrix actors.
Official core also rejects nonassignable internal policies; preserving the existing root guard does not by itself establish every policy-name restriction is equivalent.
Any new stored field requires explicit migration/state-fence review and constructor coverage; no compile/runtime validation is claimed here.
Do not add default to test actors or relax global ACL negative tests to conceal the divergence.
New meaningful storage/issuance/root/renewal regression names must be listed separately; the existing 23 and 237/254 denominators are not silently changed.
